docTitle: Pail · Open-source S3 client for Windows, macOS and Linux
docDescription: Free, open-source desktop app and command line for Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO and other S3-compatible storage. Browse, transfer and sync files.
heroTitle: A desktop client for S3‑compatible storage
heroSub: Browse buckets, move files, manage versions and bucket settings, share links. Free and open source for Windows, macOS and Linux.
shotAlt: The Pail main window: bucket list, object table and inspector
providersOther: Other S3-compatible services can be added with a custom endpoint.
fTransfersBody: Upload and download files, folders or whole buckets, or drag files into the window. Queues show progress and speed; cancel or retry any item. Large files go up in parts with checksums.
fVersionsBody: See every version of an object, download or restore one, undo a delete, and permanently remove only the versions you pick.
fAccountsBody: Access keys, AWS profiles, the default credential chain, AssumeRole or anonymous access. For other services, set the endpoint, region and path-style addressing, and test the connection.
fSettingsBody: 14 settings, including versioning, encryption, policy, CORS, lifecycle and replication, as a form or as JSON.
fPropsBody: Headers, metadata, tags, ACL, storage class and server-side encryption for one object or a selection.
fSyncBody: Upload, download or mirror a folder. Compare by size and time, size or checksum, exclude files by pattern, and review the plan first.
fLinksBody: Presigned GET or PUT links with an expiry, for one object or many. With a CDN domain on the account, copy the CDN link after an upload.
fRulesBody: Match a bucket and key pattern to set headers, storage class and encryption on upload, or to compress with GZIP, ZIP or AES-256 ZIP.
cliBody: pail uses the same accounts and saved sync jobs as the desktop app. Add --json for machine-readable output.
privacyLede: Pail has no telemetry and does not check for updates.
pNetBody: Pail connects only to the storage endpoints of the accounts you add.
pKeysBody: Secret keys go to Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain or the Linux Secret Service. Without a keychain, use the encrypted vault.
pLogBody: The log is off until you turn it on. Signatures, Authorization headers, query strings and known secrets are removed before anything is written.
pScopeBody: Destructive actions list what they will affect before they run. To delete a bucket, you type its name.
sourceGithubNote: Files are served from GitHub Releases.
sourceMirrorNote: Files are served from pan.zsh.moe, a copy of the same release. Check them against SHA256SUMS.
mirrorFallback: The same files are on the mirror:
osMacReq: macOS 11 or later · .zip with Pail.app and pail
osLinuxReq: .tar.gz with pail-desktop, pail, a .desktop file and an icon
downloadNote: The downloads are not code-signed, so macOS and Windows may warn you the first time you open Pail.
demoLede: A 48-second tour: browse a bucket, upload files, share a link, restore an older version.
demoNote: The window is the real app on a demo server with sample data. The titles and the flying files are added.

docStartDesc: How to install Pail, add an account and use the command line, where Pail keeps your data, and which platforms and services are tested.
docCliDesc: Reference for the pail command line: global flags, commands, CDN URLs, the encrypted vault, output, exit codes and limits.
docChangelogDesc: What changed in each Pail release, and the known limitations.
